To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Wolter I optics model in Geant4 can be used to estimate the focusing performances of the eXTP optics, and that the multiple scattering model of charged particles at high grazing incidence can be used instead with a reasonable accuracy and CPU time.

we have developed a Geant4 simulation for eXTP Wolter I type focusing mirrors, including the responses of X rays and charged particle scattering, which will be useful for eXTP mirror optimization and background estimation.

a geometrical and physical simulation model of Wolter type I optics is implemented in Geant, which can simultaneously simulate the responses to X ray photons and charged particles, and the multiple scattering model provided in Geant can be used instead with reasonable accuracy and cost when the step length is properly constrained.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the simulation of the mirror responses to photons and particles, which is essential for the design of eXTP and the analysis of its data.
the development of a Geant4 model for the simulation of X ray focusing optics and the validation of this model.
the development of a simulation tool to study the responses of Wolter I mirrors to X ray and charged particles, which is a key step to the optimization of the eXTP mirror design.

the Geant4 simulation can be used as a reliable tool to predict the focusing performance and radiation background of the Wolter I mirrors for the eXTP mission.
the simulation model developed here is a powerful tool for eXTP design, and can be used as a reference for similar applications.
Geant4 can be used to simulate the responses of Wolter I mirrors to X rays and particles.

the Geant4 simulation for Wolter I optics is now ready for the design of eXTP, and can be applied to other Wolter I optics missions.

the Geant4 toolkit can be used to simulate the mirror responses of the eXTP observatory.
